request.user:
Change c0332. Location: 1818 Vol. II, Ch. IX; 1831 Ch. XVII.

Context before (unchanged): Saying this, he suddenly quitted me, fearful, perhaps, of any change in my sentiments.

1818 text: I saw him descend the mountain with greater speed than the flight of an eagle, and quickly lost him among the undulations of the sea of ice.

1831 text: I saw him descend the mountain with greater speed than the flight of an eagle, and quickly lost among the undulations of the sea of ice.

Diff: I saw him descend the mountain with greater speed than the flight of an eagle, and quickly lost [-him-] among the undulations of the sea of ice.

Context after (unchanged): His tale had occupied the whole day; and the sun was upon the verge of the horizon when he departed.

result.rationale: Removal of the object pronoun 'him' in 'quickly lost him' to 'quickly lost' is a grammatical tightening with no change to events or meaning; the sense of losing sight of the creature remains.
